subject: Structuring SKU credits and technical framing for batching / KV-cache / quantization

Hi Aditya / Laura,

Thanks for the initial deck. A couple of clarifying points from our side to help procurement and engineering align:

- Workload profile: production search/RAG (user queries -> retrieval -> LLM generate). Avg seq length ~120 tokens, p50 latency target ~150ms, p95 ~400ms (tight for web UI).
- Monthly request mix: 60% short chats (<=50 tokens), 30% medium (50-250), 10% long (>250).
- We need guidance on: how to trade committed credits vs per-SKU pricing, and what "KV-cache credits" mean in practice. Also want to understand quantization risk on hallucination-sensitive prompts.

Procurement asks: can you map proposed credits to an estimated monthly $ spend range and confirm whether unused committed credits can be rolled into a following quarter for pilots?

I'm attaching our usage snapshot. We have a short window — procurement would like a firm commercial structure by Aug 26 to include in Q4 planning.

Thanks,
Claire

Claire — great context, thanks. High level proposal attached (edgeapps_mop_v1.xlsx) plus a brief KV cache benchmark (kv_cache_benchmark.pdf). Summary below; will schedule a short call to walk through numbers.

1) Commercial framing (pilot -> scale):
   - Pilot (90 days): modest committed credits (50k credits) + per-token overage. Pilot credits are refundable only as consumption (i.e., non-refundable monetary credit but can be applied to future quarters once you convert to a paid reserved capacity contract). For procurement: we can offer one-time rollover for the next quarter for pilots.
   - Scale: Commit + SKU mapping (differentiated credits for Tiny/Small/Base/Opt models). Credits convert to effective tokens based on quantization & cache; we include conversion tables in the attachment.

2) SKU / credit mapping idea (technical rationale):
   - Split traffic by inference pattern: short-chat, retrieval-augmented (RAG) medium, long-batched jobs.
   - Offer "hot-prefix KV credits": these represent the number of unique prefixes that can be served from memory with near-zero token cost. Example: 1k hot-prefix credits ~= sustaining 5k queries/day with prefix hits.

3) Batching & latency guardrails:
   - For your p50/p95 targets we recommend conservative batching (max batch size 8–16 depending on model) and dynamic latency SLO routing.
   - Batching reduces per-token cost ~15–35% depending on sequence length distribution — we modeled that in the spreadsheet. Note: larger batch sizes increase tail-latency for single-user interactive flows.

4) Quantization guidance:
   - Recommendation: evaluate 4-bit (nf4 / 4-bit asymmetric) for the medium / long inference where quality regressions are minimal after our standard calibration. Use fp16 for the short-chat path where hallucination risk is higher.
   - We include a quick A/B eval protocol in the spreadsheet so you can validate on your prompt set before rolling.

Next steps: 30-minute call to agree on credit bands + one sample mapping that ties your current usage snapshot to expected monthly spend ranges. Can you do Aug 24 or 25?

— Aditya
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Claire, quick technical note to make the conversion transparent for procurement:

- Baseline: 1 credit = ~1 inference-token at fp16 baseline (this is what we use for public-facing pricing).
- Quantized multiplier: when using 4-bit quantization, effective token cost is reduced by ~2.4x (varies by model and sequence length). So 1 committed credit would cover ~2.4 tokens of equivalent fp16 work.
- KV cache: we bill "hot-prefix units" not raw tokens — because a hit avoids decoding N tokens entirely. Billing example (from spreadsheet):

   Example projection (monthly)
   - Total input tokens (decoded): 180M
   - Estimated cache hits: 28% (hot prefixes) -> tokens avoided: ~50M
   - Effective token billable after quantization: (180M - 50M) / 2.4 ~= 54M credits

- Batching impact: average batch factor of 5 lowers per-token compute by ~20% relative to single-shot. We model combined effect as: credits_needed = (decoded_tokens - cache_savings) / quant_multiplier / batching_factor.

We left a cell in the spreadsheet where you can plug real cache-hit % and batch factor; swapping quant profiles shows the delta immediately. Happy to run a quick sensitivity table during the call.

— PrIyom
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Aditya / team — thanks for the clarity. A couple of procurement-specific questions before we lock calendar:

1) SLA: if we commit to the scale SKU mapping, what are typical latency and availability SLOs we can expect for the short-chat path vs the batch path? Need numbers we can include in an internal packet.
2) Credits: is there a mechanism to reclassify unused pilot credits into a sustained discount if we convert to a yearly reserved contract within 60 days of pilot end?

Also, curious whether the KV cache "hot-prefix units" can be scoped per environment (staging vs prod) or would they be shared under a single account-level allotment?

Procurement timeline: we still need a signed shape by Aug 26 to make our Q4 planning. Can we get a short note tying your commercial proposal to the SLA / refund/rollover language?

Samir — thanks, short answers + next steps below. We'll follow up with a one-page commercial addendum and an SLA snippet you can share with procurement.

1) Typical SLOs (what we commit to in Dedicated contracts):
   - Short-chat (interactive path): p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 400ms (dependent on model choice; we route to lower-latency variants and keep smaller batch caps).
   - Batch / long jobs: p50 <= 800ms (higher throughput optimized), p95 <= 2s.
   - Availability: 99.9% for Dedicated; higher SLAs available with premium support.

2) Credits & rollover:
   - Pilot credit rollover: we can include a one-time rollover of unused pilot credits into the next quarter if you convert to a 12-month reserved contract within 60 days of pilot close.
   - Reclassification to sustained discount: yes — if you convert to an annual commit within the 60-day window, we can apply a conversion multiplier that effectively increases the value of remaining pilot credits (we'll show math in the addendum).

3) KV cache scoping:
   - Hot-prefix units are assigned at account level but can be logically partitioned by environment in the Console. For strict separation we support per-namespace allocations for Dedicated customers.

Next steps: Laura / Kimberly will draft the one-page addendum + SLA snippet and share a DocuSign link. Proposed call: Aug 26 10:00am PT to walk the spreadsheet and lock bands. Please confirm availability.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out quickly.

— Aditya
